review_text: "Before you fall for the tempting specs of the new Edge 70 Fusion—like its massive 7000 mAh battery, 1.5K quad-curved display, or premium design—please read this warning. I am writing this because I bought its predecessor, the Moto Edge 50 Fusion, on Amazon in January 2025. It looked like a premium champion on day one, but it hid a critical hardware vulnerability that turned it into a completely useless paperweight right after the warranty ended. My Experience with Motorola Quality: The Sudden Glitch: In May 2026 (just 16 months of very careful use), my phone's screen completely went white. No touch response, no recovery—it completely bricked out of nowhere. The 'Moto Care' Shrug: I took it to an official authorized service center. They didn't even run a deep diagnostic. They took one look at the white screen and immediately declared it a motherboard failure. Zero Accountability: Their exact response was: 'If this happened within 1 year, we would replace it. But since your warranty is over, nothing can be done.' No solutions, no component discounts. A total loss of ₹20K+ in under 1.5 years. Why You Should Hesitate Before Buying the Edge 70 Fusion: Unresolved Hardware Cycles: Online tech forums and community threads are packed with users facing this exact same screen flickering, white screen, and sudden motherboard loop. It points to a serious long-term component optimization issue in Moto's mid-range lineup. Exorbitant Repair Costs: If your Edge 70 Fusion suffers a motherboard breakdown out of warranty, the official repair will cost you nearly as much as the phone itself. No Support Past Day 365: Moto Care will completely abandon you the exact day your 12-month standard warranty expires, leaving you to bear a 100% financial loss. Final Verdict: A phone is an investment that should easily last 2 to 3 years. Motorola has completely lost my trust. Don't risk your hard-earned money on flashy designs; look at brands with proven long-term durability and cooperative post-warranty customer support."
